body.statement:
For each fixed \(P_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal F_s)\), there are a class-wide constant \(C_1>0\) and center-dependent constants \(c_0(P_0)>0\) and \(\kappa(P_0)>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb E_P\lVert\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\rVert^2
\leq C_1\frac{L_n}{n}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), and
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{n}{L_n}
\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa(P_0))}
\mathbb E_P\lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P)\rVert^2
\geq c_0(P_0).
\]
The lower bound is witnessed by def:green-local-alternatives and lem:green-local-alternatives, for which \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)=(\eta/a_h)L_n\).  The upper bound remains the uniform assertion over \(\mathcal F_s\).
body.justification: The established alternatives prove the local logarithmic lower rate; the plug-in upper second moment still needs the coupled mixed expansion and tail control.
body.gap: A lower bound and weak convergence cannot substitute for a class-uniform upper-risk proof.
body.consumer: Only the converse half of the claimed rate match is currently supported.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove the class-uniform upper second-moment bound for the specified plug-in under the corrected coupled expansion.
obligation.obstruction: The established Green alternatives prove the local lower rate, but the upper bound requires integrated control of the unresolved mixed nonlinear remainder and bounded fallback event. Weak convergence would not suffice.
obligation.attempted: The two-point Hellinger testing argument was completed from the established alternatives, and the upper bound was reduced to the mixed expansion and its tail moments.
obligation.partial_result:
The lower half of the risk claim follows from the already established Green alternatives.  Let
\[
 \Delta_n=\left\lvert\upsilon^{\mathsf T}
 \{\tau(P_{n,+})-\tau(P_{n,-})\}_1\right\rvert.
\]
The established separation and \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)=(\eta/a_h)L_n\) give
\[
 \Delta_n^2\geq c(P_0)\zeta^2\frac{L_n}{n}.
\tag{16}
\]
For any estimator, testing according to which of the two scalar parameters is closer shows
\[
 \max_{\sigma\in\{+,-\}}
 \mathbb E_{P_{n,\sigma}}\lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P_{n,\sigma})\rVert^2
 \geq \frac{\Delta_n^2}{8}
 \left(1-\operatorname{TV}(P_{n,+}^{\otimes},P_{n,-}^{\otimes})\right).
\tag{17}
\]
The established product-Hellinger bound is at most \(1/2\); choosing the fixed amplitude smaller if necessary bounds the total variation in (17) strictly below one.  Equations (16)--(17) prove a positive lower constant after multiplication by \(n/L_n\).  The class-uniform upper bound is still open because it needs the coupled mixed stochastic expansion and its integrated-tail control; weak convergence alone cannot supply the required second moment.
